short: A short transitional age between the Ice Age hunters and the first farmers.
full:
The Mesolithic is the bridge between the Palaeolithic and the Neolithic, running roughly from 12,000 to 10,000 BCE in the Near East and considerably later in northern Europe. As the glaciers withdrew, tundra gave way to forest, the great herds thinned, and people adapted to a patchier, more varied set of resources.

Its signature technology is the microlith: tiny worked flints hafted in rows to make composite arrows, harpoons and sickles. Coastal and riverine sites become prominent, with shell middens, fish traps and the earliest known boats. Communities became more sedentary in resource-rich places, an important precondition for what followed.
